title: The Cover of Geneva Anew
premise: Zephyrine Sandoval, a fixer for the Directorate of Unrecorded Affairs — an embassy that exists on no map and no ledger — has spent two years unable to sleep through the night since the incident in Geneva that killed her handler and left a child witness missing. When a real-estate listing surfaces showing the interior of a safe house only she and three dead people ever entered, she realizes someone is selling her invisibility back to her, room by room. As she traces the listing through Zurich's gray markets, she discovers the broker is the missing child, now grown and holding the memory Zephyrine buried: proof that the Directorate itself ordered the Geneva operation's failure. The extraction flight leaves at dawn, and Zephyrine must choose between trading the secret that would destroy her employers — and free her — or protecting the institution that made her belong somewhere for the first time. She trades it, broadcasts the truth mid-flight, and lands in Reykjavík as a nameless woman who, for the first night in two years, sleeps until morning.
about_author: Jonah Okonkwo is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade moving people and secrets across European borders before turning to fiction. He writes from a different city each year, a habit he describes as 'research into belonging.'

chapters.title: Rooms Without Names
chapters.summary: Zephyrine, unable to sleep, scrolls property listings at 3 a.m. in her Lisbon apartment and finds the safe house — every room photographed, down to the scorch mark she never reported. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: dread masquerading as curiosity; the past has an address again.

chapters.title: The Directorate of Unrecorded Affairs
chapters.summary: Flashback-tinged chapter establishing her role: she cleans up the embassy that doesn't exist, erasing people from records, hotels, and memories. Her superior, Voss, assigns her to quietly acquire the listing before it spreads. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the comfort and cage of institutional belonging.

chapters.title: Seller Unknown
chapters.summary: Zephyrine flies to Geneva under a workman's identity and finds the listing agency is a shell owned by a dead man — her dead handler, Aldrich. Someone is using his corporate ghost. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; the dead don't sign contracts.

chapters.title: What the Camera Saw
chapters.summary: Examining the listing photos, Zephyrine realizes one frame shows a reflection: a figure standing where she stood the night of the incident. The photos were staged from memory — someone was there, or remembers it exactly. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: vertigo; her private guilt has a witness.

chapters.title: Voss Wants a Quiet Sale
chapters.summary: Voss instructs her to buy the property, demolish it, and burn the listing — standard erasure. But he also assigns a second operative, Marek, 'to assist.' Zephyrine recognizes a leash when she's handed one. POV: Zephyrine with a Voss interlude. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling under loyalty.

chapters.title: The Gray Market Broker
chapters.summary: Zephyrine traces the shell through a Zurich information broker who deals in 'involuntary provenance' — stolen memories, coerced testimony. The broker hints the seller is selling more than a house. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the thriller's engine turns; secrets have market value.

chapters.title: The Child in the Stairwell
chapters.summary: A memory chapter: the Geneva incident, told slantwise — the operation, the explosion, and the child Zephyrine was ordered to erase who vanished instead. She has never told anyone she let the child go. POV: Zephyrine, past tense. Emotional beat: the wound beneath the insomnia finally named.

chapters.title: Marek Follows the Money
chapters.summary: Marek, working his own angle, discovers the listing's payment trail leads to a Geneva orphanage stipend — someone has been funded for eighteen years. He reports it to Voss, not Zephyrine. POV: Marek. Emotional beat: rivalrous unease; the institution watches its own.

chapters.title: An Appointment at the Safe House
chapters.summary: A viewing appointment appears in Zephyrine's inbox, addressed to her real name — the one that officially doesn't exist. The message: 'Come see what you left behind.' She goes, against every instinct. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: terror and terrible longing braided together.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: At the safe house she meets Ilse — the child from the stairwell, now an adult, alive because Zephyrine looked away. Ilse doesn't want revenge; she wants the truth acknowledged, and she has Aldrich's final dossier as leverage. POV: Zephyrine and Ilse alternating. Emotional beat: recognition; two survivors of the same lie.

chapters.title: What Aldrich Knew
chapters.summary: Ilse reveals the dossier: the Directorate sabotaged its own Geneva operation to bury a defector's evidence, and Aldrich died trying to move it out. The 'incident' was internal housekeeping. POV: Ilse, mostly. Emotional beat: the ground tilts — Zephyrine's guilt was manufactured.

chapters.title: Terms of Sale
chapters.summary: Ilse's price: not money — acknowledgment. She wants the dossier published and her existence restored to the record, and she'll trade the only copy to Zephyrine before dawn's extraction flight. Zephyrine has until sunrise. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: a deadline with a soul attached.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Marek's report reaches Voss; Zephyrine's access is quietly revoked mid-mission — her credentials die in her hand at a Geneva tram stop. She is now exactly what she fixes: an unrecorded person. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: exile from the only belonging she had.

chapters.title: Running the Old Routes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine uses every ghost route she built for others to stay ahead of Marek's team through Geneva's night — the city she once erased people from now erasing her. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: fugitive adrenaline shot through with bitter irony.

chapters.title: The Broker's Price
chapters.summary: She returns to the Zurich broker for a way to broadcast the dossier globally in one stroke; the price is her own file — every operation she's ever cleaned. To publish the truth, she must publish herself. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the theme made literal — memory as currency.

chapters.title: Marek's Doubt
chapters.summary: Marek, tailing her, reads a fragment of the dossier and recognizes his own first mission inside it — he was the instrument of an erasure too. He hesitates at the trigger moment and lets her go. POV: Marek. Emotional beat: the corrupted faithful beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Airport at 4 A.M.
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Ilse converge on the private terminal where the extraction flight waits. Voss is there in person — he never sends, he arrives — and offers Zephyrine everything back if she hands over the dossier and Ilse. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the temptation of belonging at its most seductive.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Zephyrine makes the trade — but not the one Voss expects: she gives Ilse the broker's broadcast key and keeps the dossier herself, walking it onto the tarmac as collateral. Voss orders Marek to stop her. He doesn't. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: the climax's clean, terrifying choice.

chapters.title: Dawn, Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Aboard the flight, Zephyrine triggers the broadcast: the dossier, the listing photos, her own file — the Directorate's ledger spilled into daylight as the plane leaves Swiss airspace. Voss's voice on the satphone offers one last deal. She hangs up. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: catharsis at altitude; the secret worth killing for, spent.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Gray Airspace
chapters.summary: Consequences cascade: the embassy's shells begin collapsing, Marek disappears into the same gray routes he once patrolled, and Ilse's name — her real name — appears in the first news stories. POV: Marek and brief Voss. Emotional beat: institutions are people; some fall, some walk away.

chapters.title: A Name on a Door
chapters.summary: In Reykjavík, Zephyrine signs a lease with her true name for the first time in fifteen years and visits Ilse, who is learning to be legible to the world. They don't forgive each other yet; they agree to keep meeting. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt on truth instead of erasure.

chapters.title: The First Night
chapters.summary: Zephyrine sleeps through the night — eight unbroken hours — and wakes to a city that knows her name and doesn't care. The final image: she leaves her curtains open. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; memory kept, power refused, belonging earned.
